minimum at t 	 10 h, the optical density increased linearly over
time. This period is denoted as the linear phase. Apparently,
growth now became limited by the H2 supply. To test this, the
organism was grown at a higher gassing rate (428 ml min1).
The same growth behavior was found (Fig. 2A). Quite remark-
ably, pH2 did not drop to low values during the linear growth
stage, but it was maintained as high as 29 kPa. Again, the
hydrogen consumption rate became constant (H2 	 275 ml
min1), but the gas was only partly utilized. Further experi-
ments showed that the pH2 values could be manipulated by the
H2–CO2 gassing regimen (Table 3). Depending on the hydro-
gen mass transfer characteristics, i.e., gassing rate/culture vol-
ume ratio and mixing intensity (number of impellers), steady
pH2 values were obtained during the linear growth phase that
ranged between 1 and 59 kPa. Linear growth could proceed for
prolonged periods of time (at least 72 h), at which OD600
values of up to 7 to 10 were obtained (data not shown). Hy-
drogen consumption and methane production rates, as well as
dissolved hydrogen partial pressures, however, remained con-
stant throughout the whole period of linear growth.
